claims.text: The baseline is a nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalyst.
The intervention adds a trace amount of a metal distinct from Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os.
The selected dopant is known to shift the catalyst's d-band center.
Trace dopant addition induces a subtle shift in the d-band center of PtPdRhRuIrOs.
A shift in the d-band center changes the adsorption energies of critical ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Variation in intermediate adsorption strength can alter catalytic turnover rates.
Differences in local electronic structure in high-entropy alloys can tune reaction selectivity.
The adsorption-energy modification favors pathways producing acetic acid rather than acetaldehyde.
The doped catalyst will have a statistically significant increase in the acetic-acid-to-acetaldehyde ratio relative to the undoped catalyst.
The doped catalyst will exhibit corresponding shifts in turnover frequency.
The hypothesis is intended to hold at 50–80 °C under controlled electrochemical potentials and typical ethanol concentrations.
The magnitude of the product-distribution and turnover-frequency changes may depend on the local catalyst environment and dopant concentration.
XPS or UPS can be used to measure the proposed d-band-center shift.
Absence of statistically significant product-ratio, turnover-frequency, and d-band-center changes relative to the undoped control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline already contains six metals, so a dopant distinct from all six would be a seventh metal, not the stated 'fourth metal dopant.'

The prediction specifically requires an increase in the acetic-acid-to-acetaldehyde ratio, whereas the uncertainty statement says any statistically significant change would support the mechanism; a significant decrease would contradict the directional prediction.
